title: Henri Matisse's birth chart
metaDescription: Henri Matisse's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.9° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mercury and Uranus sit 0.1° from an exact opposition — near enough that the tradition reads thinking and disruption as a single working part. The scheme reads an opposition as a axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 9.9° Capricorn. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — a earth sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (20.3°), Venus in Aquarius (25.9°), Mars in Capricorn (25.8°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mercury to Uranus, a opposition with 0.1° of slack. Oppositions are read as full-moon geometry — maximum visibility between two needs that share one spine. Behind it, the Sun trine Jupiter at 1.1°, and Mercury square Neptune at 3.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Uranus while both square Neptune. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. Venus stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has one entry for this chart. Mars in Capricorn at 25.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 5, fire 3, air 1, water 1; modalities cardinal 5, fixed 3, mutable 2. An earth emphasis reads as trust in the tangible: the plan matters less than whether the thing stands up. Jupiter, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 20.8°.
